## Declaration

The author, Lars Schöbitz, used the AI tool Claude Code with the model claude-fable-5-1 (Anthropic) to prepare the slide deck "Git for Scientists" for the Data Stewardship Network Autumn Community Meeting at ETH Zurich on 22 September 2026. He used the tool on 21 September 2026 between 09:45 and 13:24 to turn his outline and his recorded talk into slides and speaker notes, to tighten the speaker notes, to place the images and their source lines, to write the commit messages, to generate two QR code images, and to style the deck. He wrote the outline, gave and recorded the talk twice, gathered the images, entered the references, and decided on every proposed text change. He remains responsible for all content of the deck. The deck cites no AI output as a source, and no AI is named as an author.

The author also used the same tool on 7 September 2026 for the earlier version of the deck, which he gave as a trial run. The record of that version is listed under lineage below.

## How this page was made

Claude Code generated this page on 21 September 2026 with the model claude-fable-5-1. The prompt is the one quoted on the slide "Let the AI declare your AI use" in the deck. The tool read only this repository. It used the following sources:

- the prompt files in the prompts folder,
- the git history of the deck, including the trailers in the commit messages,
- the git blame of the deck file, which names the last commit that touched each line,
- the images folder of the deck,
- the pull requests of the repository,
- the deck file itself, including its speaker notes.

The page checks the record against two documents:

- ETH Zurich, Information Security and Artificial Intelligence (AI), Guide for Users of AI at ETH Zurich, 24 July 2025 ([PDF](https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/associates/services/News/service-news/2025/09/250923-ki-leitfaden/ETH-InfoSec-AI-Guide-EN.pdf)), called the AI guide below.
- ETH Library, Zitierleitfaden der ETH Zürich, section "Generative künstliche Intelligenz", last updated 17 February 2025 ([PDF](https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/associates/ethlibrary-dam/documents/ETH-Zuerich_Zitierleitfaden.pdf)), called the citation guide below.

The author reviewed the page before committing it. The prompt that produced the page is added to the prompts folder at commit, so the generation of the declaration is itself part of the record.

## What the page covers

The page covers the file `slides/dsn-agentsforsci.qmd` at commit 643d506 of 21 September 2026, 13:45, plus the edits in the working tree at the time of generation. The uncommitted edits change seven lines. They replace two "TODO" markers with hand icons on the poll slides, rename one slide title, and put the full prompt on the slide "Let the AI declare your AI use". No prompt file covers the uncommitted edits.

The deck replaced an earlier deck, `slides/dsn-autumn-2026.qmd`, which the author gave as a trial run at the Global Health Engineering weekly on 7 September 2026. The two decks share the reference file `slides/dsn-autumn-2026.bib`.

## The record

### Tool and model

The record names one AI tool and one model.

- The tool is Claude Code by Anthropic, run in the terminal. The deck names it on the slide "Agents for Scientists" and on the slide "A commit skill". The version of Claude Code is not recorded in the repository.
- The model is claude-fable-5-1. Every prompt file records it in the field `model`, and every assisted commit records it in the trailer `Assisted-by: Claude claude-fable-5-1`.

### Pull requests

The repository has four merged pull requests, all from dev into main, opened by the author. The last one was merged on 2 July 2026. None of them covers the deck. At the time of generation the eleven commits sit on dev, which is 30 commits ahead of main, and the last four commits are not yet pushed to origin. So there is no pull request and no review comment for the deck yet.

### Lines of the deck by last commit

The git blame names the last commit that touched each line of the deck. The table counts the lines that are not blank.

| Last commit | Lines | Share |
|---|---|---|
| A commit with the Assisted-by trailer | 221 | 78% |
| A commit with no trailer | 55 | 20% |
| Uncommitted edits | 6 | 2% |
| Total | 282 | 100% |

The share of assisted lines is an upper bound of what the AI wrote, for two reasons. First, the message of commit 65d7526 says that the tool turned the author's outline into the deck. The outline came from commit f58a0b4 and had 147 lines, so lines the author wrote now show the assisted commit that reformatted them. Second, the message of commit 756ff56 says that the author's typed text became the speaker notes and that the diff carries both the tool's section build and the author's own revisions. Blame cannot separate the two.

The deck file holds 2,087 words, of which 1,050 are speaker notes.

### What the AI did

The commit messages and the prompts record the following contributions of the tool.

- It turned the author's outline and the transcript of the author's recorded run through into a reveal.js deck with speaker notes (commit 65d7526).
- It tightened the speaker notes from 937 to 744 words. The author accepted or edited each change (commit b9b94fe).
- It placed the images the author had gathered, added their source lines, and entered the event facts of the Research Data Conference 2026 from the ConfTool page (commit 276b698).
- It applied nine changes the author asked for after the talk at the weekly (commit 754eb73).
- It built the section "Declaration of AI use" from the author's outline and screenshots (commit 756ff56).
- It styled the opening slide, the four section slides, the footers, and the closing slide, and moved the site and the deck to the font Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. The commit also touched `_quarto.yml`, `theme.scss`, and `slides/slides.scss` (commit 8d84e46).
- It generated the two QR code images (commit 65d7526). The method is not recorded.
- It corrected one URL in the reference file, using the URL the author supplied in prompt 005 (commit 276b698).
- It wrote the messages of the six assisted commits.
- It transcribed two recordings of the author's talk. The commit messages call them vault voice notes 47 and 48. The recordings and transcripts are kept outside the repository.

### What the author did

The record shows the following contributions of the author.

- He wrote the outline of the deck (commit f58a0b4, 147 lines, no AI use recorded).
- He gave and recorded the talk twice, on 7 September 2026 as a trial run (commit 4087b5a) and on 21 September 2026 at the weekly (commit 754eb73), and asked for changes based on the recordings.
- He decided on all 26 proposed text changes in the two rounds of review (prompt files 004 and 010).
- He made five commits with no AI use recorded, the outline (f58a0b4) and four rounds of edits by hand (be09676, 4d65e74, 29162eb, 643d506), and he made the uncommitted edits.
- He gathered the screenshots, the painting file, the icon, and the terminal recording (commits 276b698 and 756ff56).
- He entered the six references in the reference file (commit 66547a5 of 7 September 2026, no AI use recorded).
- He wrote the ten prompts.

### Facts entered through assisted commits

The AI guide asks users to review all results of the AI for accuracy before they use them in a presentation. The following facts entered the deck through assisted commits. The author is responsible for checking them against the named source.

- The Research Data Conference 2026 takes place on 19 and 20 November 2026 on the Gurten in Bern. The workshop runs on Friday 20 November from 9:30 to 11:30 and lasts 120 minutes. The commit message names the ConfTool session page as the source (commit 276b698).
- Single factor papers from the NHANES database went from about 4 a year to 190 in 2024. The commit message attributes the count to Suchak et al. (commit 754eb73). The reference file holds the entry suchak2025explosion, which the author entered, but the deck does not cite it, so the count stands in the speaker notes without a reference.
- The speaker notes went from 937 to 744 words (commit b9b94fe).

The claim of a paper in 30 minutes and the other slide content came from the author's outline and talk, and the two works the deck cites, spick2026thirtyminute and barnett2026armsrace, are entries the author entered in the reference file.

## What the record does not show

- The recordings and transcripts of the talk, called vault voice notes 38, 47, and 48 in the commit messages, are kept outside the repository.
- The version of Claude Code and its settings, including the interaction history and the training opt out, are not in the repository.
- Whether Claude Code is on the ETH list of approved external cloud services is not in the repository.
- The method used to generate the two QR codes is not recorded.
- The images pasted into prompts 001 and 009 are not kept.
- The prompt files of 7 September 2026 carry approximate timestamps, as their frontmatter says.
- Five commits and the uncommitted edits carry no trailer and no prompt file. The record shows no AI use for them and cannot prove there was none.
- Inside an assisted commit, blame cannot separate the tool's text from the author's edits.
- The time the author and the tool spent is not recorded.

## Lineage: the earlier deck of 7 September 2026

The earlier deck, `slides/dsn-autumn-2026.qmd`, was given as a trial run at the Global Health Engineering weekly on 7 September 2026. Its record has eleven prompt files and four commits. The prompt timestamps are approximate, as their frontmatter says.

| Commit | Time | Subject | Trailer | Prompt files |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a7a8b2e | 10:24 | prepare slides outline for DSN event | none | none |
| 66547a5 | 10:24 | add literature for DSN talk | none | none |
| 4087b5a | 13:07 | docs(slides): DSN 2026 deck as used in trial run | Human-authored and Assisted-by | 001 to 010 |
| f08c1bc | 13:07 | docs(slides): record trial run learnings in the deck | Assisted-by | 011 |

The tool prepared three outlines from the author's notes, worked the author's own outline into a deck with image placeholders, completed the header, and after the trial run wrote the timing and the learnings into a source comment of the file. The commit 4087b5a carries both trailers because the diff held the tool's work and the author's own edits. The author's reference file from commit 66547a5 is the one the current deck uses.
